result:
The project is now on the new-project path: we rank outcomes first, and stages come after.

## Outcome candidates (unranked)

I drew these from the spec's R1–R11 and §2.1. R5 (one shared code path) and R11 (defaults are reviewed config) describe how the system is built, not what you get. I folded them into the outcomes they constrain.

| # | Outcome | From | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | A Parquet filing-index catalog for a chosen range of archived quarters, built from real SEC quarterly master indexes | R1, R3 | **Requests:** under a minute of request time at 3 req/s. 1993Q1–2026Q4 is 136 quarters, at about one listing plus one file each, so roughly 270 requests. **Bytes:** unknown until a size lookup. I can read the `full-index` listing if you say yes. |
| O2 | Daily indexes added on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs and across quarter boundaries | R2 | Small: about one file per business day, 250 a year. Per-file size comes from the same lookup. |
| O3 | Original SEC bytes kept, so a parser change rebuilds the catalog without re-downloading | R6 | **Storage:** about the raw volume of O1 plus O2, retained under the retention policy. |
| O4 | Weekly reconciliation that applies SEC's later corrections, and holds any closed-quarter withdrawal for your hash-bound approval | R7, R10 | **Requests:** about 136 per run. **Your time:** one approval per gated quarter. How often the SEC changes closed quarters can only be measured by running it. |
| O5 | Readers get only complete, versioned quarters through one active pointer, never half-written files | R9 | Negligible compute. |
| O6 | All SEC traffic goes through one throttled downloader with one 3 req/s budget, shared by backfill, daily and reconciliation | R8, R11 | Sets the time floor for O1, O2 and O4 (arithmetic above). |
| O7 | Runs on Azure: ADF schedules, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, and Monitor alerts with runbooks | R4, §4.7, §8 | **Azure dollars:** not estimable without a real run, so its first stage measures it. |

## Proposed tracks

- **Track A — Filing-index catalog (O1–O6). Known progression.** The spec's §4 names these steps in order, from parse and publish through replay, daily, throttling and reconciliation.
- **Track B — Azure deployment (O7). Known progression,** following the spec's §7 phases.
- **Why split them:** a working catalog stands without Azure, and the platform choice stands without any particular catalog feature. Joining them would make the first usable catalog wait on ADF, identities and infrastructure-as-code. The split also matters because R4 is "subject to ADR acceptance", and the ADR is still Proposed.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`).
- A uv workspace with four scaffold packages: client, download, index-ingest and ingest.

Neither the spec nor the ADR is accepted yet. So I'm not treating Azure as decided; tell me if it is.

One fact for later: §4.9 places everything in a single `sec-edgar-ingest` package, but the scaffold has four packages. That belongs to the first stage's design session, not to this ranking.

## Roadmap name

`specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md`, from the spec's stem.

## Optional probe

I can do a read-only size lookup on SEC's `full-index` and `daily-index` listings to firm up the byte estimates. It sends a User-Agent, which the SEC requires to carry an organization name and contact email. I'd need you to give me that identity; I won't fill it in myself.

## One request

Please:
1. Rank the outcomes within Track A.
2. Rank Track A against Track B.
3. Confirm or change the tracks and their kinds.

Also tell me whether to run the probe.
